32241.sol: The emission spectrum of a element is the spectrum of frequencies of electromagnetic radiation emitted due to an atom or molecule making a transition from a high energy state to a lower energy state. 71130.subject: Biology
71130.text: Human immunodeficiency virus parasitizes which of the following cells?
71130.sol: Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV) specifically targets and parasitizes helper T cells in the human immune system. Helper T cells are also known as T ₄ lymphocytes or CD4+ T cells because they possess CD4 receptors on their surface. The virus uses these receptors to attach to and enter the host cell. options: Both statement I and statement II are correct.
Both statement I and statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but statement II is correct.
71403.sol: Statement I is incorrect because the fusion of two compatible gametes is a characteristic of sexual reproduction, not asexual reproduction. Asexual reproduction does not involve the fusion of gametes. Statement II is correct because asexual reproduction involves a single parent and produces offspring that are genetically and morphologically identical to each other and to the parent, often referred to as clones. Answer: Statement I is incorrect but statement II is correct.

109028.subject: Chemistry

109505.subject: Chemistry

121244.subject: Botany

options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion
If assertion is true but reason is false
If both assertion and reason are false
121244.sol: Classification involves hierarchy of steps, in which each step represents a rank or category, called taxonomic category or taxon. All taxa together constitute a taxonomic hierarchy as follows: Species Genus Family Order Class Phylum or division Kingdom. Most common characters among individual members are found in taxon species. Common characters decrease from species to kingdom and members of a kingdom have least number of common characters. Similarly, complexity of classification decreases from species to kingdom

121370.subject: Botany
121370.text: Viruses have which type of structure outside the cell of the host?
121370.sol: Viruses did not find a place in classification since they are not considered truly ‘living’, if we understand living as those organisms that have a cell structure. The viruses are non-cellular organisms that are characterised by having an inert crystalline structure outside the living cell.

121546.subject: Botany
121546.text: Select the correct statements among the following.
options: Polluted water bodies usually have a very high abundance of plants like Nostoc and Oscillitoria.
Diatoms are also called as ‘pearls of the ocean’
Neurospora - an ascomycetes fungus has been used as a biological tool
121546.sol: Neurospora - an ascomycetes fungus has been used as a biological tool to understand the mechanism of plant genetics. Diatoms are majorly phytoplankton which are the chief producers of the ocean. Hence known as “pearls of oceans”. Polluted water bodies are rich in nutrients especially in nitrogen content which provides favourable condition to algae like Nostoc and Oscillotoria to bloom in the water bodies.

121604.subject: Botany
options: bacteria whose DNA is relaxed or supercoiled but which have a cytoskeleton as well as mitochondria
bacteria that contain a cytoskeleton and ribosomes and endoplasmic reticulum
archaebacteria that contain protein homologous to eukaryotic core histones
archaebacteria that lack any histones resembling those found in eukaryotes but whose DNA is supercoiled.
121604.sol: Thermococcus, Methanococcus and Methanobacterium exemplify archaebacteria that lack any histones resembling those found in eukaryotes but whose DNA is negatively supercoiled. Archaebacteria do not have a nucleus, the genetic material floats freely in the cytoplasm. They consist of ribosomal RNA. DNA contains a single, circular molecule, which is compact and tightly wound. No protein is associated with DNA. The archaebacterial cell may contain plasmids, which are small, circular pieces of DNA and have a highly negat

122004.subject: Botany
122004.text: What is the basis of classification of algae?
options: on the basis of size of plant
on the basis of nature of plant
122004.sol: The algae are classified on the basis of chlorophyll present in algae. They are classified into three main classes: Chlorophyceae, Phaeophyceae and Rhodophyceae.

122243.subject: Botany
122243.text: What type of animals are Hemichordates?
122243.sol: Hemichordates have a rudimentary structure in the collar region called stomochord, a structure similar to notochord. Hemichordata was earlier considered as a sub-phylum under phylum Chordata, but now it is placed as a separate phylum under non-chordata. Hemichordates are worm-like marine animals with organ-system level of organization. Animals belonging to the phylum Chordata are bilaterally symmetrical, triploblastic, coelomate with organ-system level of organization. Animals belonging to phylum Chordata are funda

122281.subject: Botany
122281.text: What is the number of chambers in a mammal's heart?
122281.sol: The most unique mammalian characteristic is the presence of milk producing glands (mammary glands) by which the young ones are nourished. Mammals have two pairs of limbs, adapted for walking, running,climbing, burrowing, swimming or flying. Mammals have a four-chambered heart .Sexes are separate in mammals and fertilization is internalViviparous - Macropus (Kangaroo), Pteropus (Flying fox), Camelus (Camel), Macaca (Monkey), Rattus (Rat), Canis (Dog), Felis (Cat), Elephas (Elephant),Equus (Horse), Delphinus (Common

122318.subject: Botany
122318.text: Select the correct statements about this organism.
options: Teeth are modified cycloid scales which are backwardly directed.
122318.sol: Mouth is located ventrally. Teeth are modified placoid scales which are backwardly directed. They are cold-blooded (poikilothermous) animals.

122445.subject: Botany
122445.text: Anatomical features Phylum A. Osculum 1. Platyhelminthes B. Cnidoblasts 2. Cnidarians C. Comb plates 3. Ctenophores D. Flame cells 4. Sponges
122445.sol: The osculum is found in sponges. Cnidoblasts are characteristic of cnidarians. Comb plates are found in ctenophores. Flame cells are present in platyhelminthes.

122871.subject: Botany
122871.text: Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option. Assertion: In the hypogynous flower the gynoecium occupies the highest position while the other parts are situated below it. Reason: The examples of hypogynous flower are mustard, China rose and brinjal.
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion

122871.sol: In the hypogynous flower, the gynoecium occupies the highest position while the other parts are situated below it. The examples are mustard, China rose and brinjal.

123377.subject: Botany
123377.text: Components of dicot root Functions A. Epiblema 1. Initiates lateral roots and vascular cambium B. Cortex 2. Outermost layer with unicellular root hairs C. Endodermis 3. Thin-walled parenchyma cells, contains casparian strips D. Pericycle 4. Several layers of thin-walled parenchyma cells
123377.sol: Epiblema is the outermost layer with root hairs, cortex consists of thin-walled parenchyma cells, endodermis has casparian strips, and pericycle initiates lateral roots and vascular cambium.

123379.subject: Botany
123379.text: Vascular Bundle Types Examples A. Radial Vascular Bundles 1. Sunflower root B. Conjoint Open Vascular Bundles 2. Monocot stems C. Conjoint Closed Vascular Bundles 3. Common in stems and leaves D. Dicotyledonous Vascular Bundles 4. Roots
123379.sol: Radial vascular bundles are found in roots. Conjoint open vascular bundles are not specifically given as examples but typically occur in dicot stems. Conjoint closed vascular bundles are found in monocot stems, and dicotyledonous vascular bundles are common in stems and leaves.

124114.subject: Botany
124114.text: What structure is labeled as b and mentions its correct function?
options: Stroma, contains enzymes required for the synthesis of only proteins.
Granum ,contains enzymes required for the synthesis of only proteins.
Cytoplasm, contains enzymes required for the synthesis of carbohydrates and proteins
Stroma, contains enzymes required for the synthesis of proteins and carbohydrates
124114.sol: The stroma of the chloroplast contains enzymes required for the synthesis of carbohydrates and proteins.

124336.subject: Botany
124336.text: Match List-I with List-II regarding the components of the endomembrane system and their functions. List-I List-II (A) Rough ER (I) Synthesis of steroidal hormones (B) Smooth ER (II) Intracellular digestion (C) Golgi apparatus (III) Formation of glycoproteins (D) Lysosomes (IV) Protein synthesis and secretion Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
124336.sol: The endomembrane system includes the endoplasmic reticulum, Golgi complex, lysosomes, and vacuoles. Rough endoplasmic reticulum (RER) bears ribosomes on its surface and is actively involved in protein synthesis and secretion. Smooth endoplasmic reticulum (SER) is the major site for the synthesis of lipids. In animal cells, lipid-like steroidal hormones are synthesized in SER. The Golgi apparatus principally performs the function of packaging materials and is the important site of formation of glycoproteins and glyc

124356.subject: Botany
124356.text: A researcher observes two different types of cells. Cell X contains only 70S ribosomes, whereas Cell Y contains both 70S and 80S ribosomes. Identify the correct statement regarding these cells.
options: Cell X possesses a well-defined nuclear envelope.
Cell Y has naked, circular DNA as its primary genetic material.
Cell X contains mitochondria for cellular respiration.
Cell Y possesses membrane-bound organelles which are absent in Cell X.
124356.sol: Cell X contains only 70S ribosomes, which indicates it is a prokaryotic cell. Prokaryotes lack a nuclear envelope and membrane-bound organelles such as mitochondria. Cell Y contains both 70S and 80S ribosomes, indicating it is a eukaryotic cell (80S ribosomes are found in the cytoplasm and 70S ribosomes are found inside semi-autonomous organelles like mitochondria or plastids). Eukaryotic cells possess an endomembrane system and other membrane-bound organelles, which are absent in prokaryotic cells. Their primary g

124378.subject: Botany
124378.sol: Golgi apparatus or Golgi complex is absent in prokaryotic cells (PPLO, bacteria and blue-green algae). It is present in all eukaryotic cells except sieve tubes of plants, sperms of bryophytes and pteridophytes and red blood corpuscles of mammals.

124543.subject: Botany
124543.text: What major group of PGR was first isolated by F.W. Went?
124543.sol: All this started with the observation of Charles Darwin and his son Francis Darwin when they observed that the coleoptiles of canary grass responded to unilateral illumination by growing towards the light source (phototropism). Auxin was isolated by F.W. Went from tips of coleoptiles of oat seedlings.

124562.subject: Botany
124562.text: Which fruit is specifically mentioned as having flowering promoted by auxins?
124562.sol: Auxins promote flowering e.g. in pineapples. They help to initiate rooting in stem cuttings, an application widely used for plant propagation.They help to prevent fruit and leaf drop at early stages but promote the abscission of older mature leaves and fruits.

124875.subject: Botany
124875.text: Which of the following helps in ascent of sap?
124875.sol: Water is mainly absorbed by roots which goes upwards so as to replace water loss in transpiration and to be used in photosynthesis. This upward movement of water from roots to leaves through stem against force of gravity is called ascent of sap. Different theories have been put forward in support of ascent of sap. They include root pressure theory, capillary theory and transpiration pull theory. Root pressure is developed when rate of absorption is more than rate of transpiration and so water is pushed up in the tr

124883.subject: Botany
124883.text: Assertion : A plant girdled upto bast will die. Reason : Food transportation in such plant will cease followed by ceasation of water transport.
options: If both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is the correct explantion of Assertion
If both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
If Assertion is true but Reason is false
If Assertion is false but Reason is true.
124883.sol: A plant girdled upto bast will show below the girdled part, the non transportation of the food which occurs through phloem (bast). Water transport from roots to other plant parts via xylem will continue till root cells do not die due to starvation.

124914.subject: Botany
124914.text: Which macromolecule is usually oxidized to release energy during respiration?
124914.sol: Photosynthesis, of course, takes place within the chloroplasts (in the eukaryotes), whereas the breakdown of complex molecules to yield energy takes place in the cytoplasm and in the mitochondria (also only in eukaryotes). The breaking of the C-C bonds of complex compounds through oxidation within the cells, leading to release of a considerable amount of energy is called respiration. The compounds that are oxidized during this process are known as respiratory substrates. Usually carbohydrates are oxidized to releas

125058.subject: Botany
125058.text: Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option. Assertion: Animals are heterotrophic, i.e., they obtain food from plants directly or indirectly. Reason: Saprophytes like fungi are dependent on dead and decaying matter.
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but the Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
125058.sol: Animals are heterotrophic, i.e., they obtain food from plants directly or indirectly. Saprophytes like fungi are dependent on dead and decaying matter.

125087.subject: Botany

Both Assertion and Reason are false
125087.sol: The F1 headpiece is a peripheral membrane protein complex and contains the site for synthesis of ATP from ADP and inorganic phosphate. F0 is an integral membrane protein complex that forms the channel through which protons cross the inner membrane.

125167.subject: Botany
125167.text: Match List-I with List-II. List-I (Respiratory Substrate) List-II (RQ Value) (A) Carbohydrates (I) 0.9 (B) Proteins (II) 0.7 (C) Tripalmitin (III) 1.0 Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
125167.sol: The respiratory quotient (RQ) is the ratio of the volume of CO₂ evolved to the volume of O₂ consumed during respiration. For carbohydrates, the RQ value is 1.0 because equal volumes of CO₂ and O₂ are evolved and consumed, respectively. When proteins are used as respiratory substrates, the RQ value is approximately 0.9 . For fats like tripalmitin, the RQ value is less than 1 , specifically 0.7 . Therefore, the correct matching is (A)-(III), (B)-(I), (C)-(II). Answer: (A)-(III), (B)-(I), (C)-(II)

125183.subject: Botany
125183.text: Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R). Assertion (A): The Respiratory Quotient (RQ) of tripalmitin is less than one. Reason (R): Fats contain less oxygen in their molecular structure compared to carbohydrates, hence they require more external oxygen for complete oxidation. 125183.sol: The Respiratory Quotient (RQ) is the ratio of the volume of CO₂ evolved to the volume of O₂ consumed in respiration. Tripalmitin is a fat. The RQ of fats is less than 1 (specifically 0.7 for tripalmitin). Thus, the Assertion is correct. Fats have a highly reduced state and contain very little oxygen in their molecular structure compared to carbohydrates. Consequently, during aerobic respiration, they require a larger volume of external oxygen to completely oxidize the carbon and hydrogen atoms into CO₂ and H₂O . Si

125327.sol: A milestone contribution to the understanding of photosynthesis was that made by a microbiologist, Cornelius van Niel (1897-1985), who, based on his studies of purple and green bacteria, demonstrated that photosynthesis is essentially a light-dependent reaction in which hydrogen from a suitable oxidisable compound reduces carbon dioxide to carbohydrates. In green plants H2O is the hydrogen donor and is oxidised to O2 . Some organisms do not release O2 during photosynthesis. When H2 S, instead is the hydrogen donor

125598.subject: Botany

options: ATP is produced in cyclic photophosphorylation while ATP and NADPH2 is produced in non-cyclic photophosphoryla
Cyclic photophosphorylation occurs both in photosystem -1 & 2 while non-cyclic photophosphorylation occurs onl
Photolysis of water occurs in Cyclic photophosphorylation while Photolysis of water does not occur in non-cycl
125598.sol: ATP is produced in cyclic photophosphorylation while ATP and NADPH2 is produced in noncyclic photophosphorylation is the difference between cyclic and non-cyclic photophosphorylation.

125649.subject: Botany
125649.text: If a healthy, actively photosynthesizing plant is suddenly transferred from a well-lit environment into a completely dark room, what will be the immediate to short-term fate of the biosynthetic phase (sugar synthesis) in its leaves?
options: It continues indefinitely because the biosynthetic phase is completely independent of light
It stops immediately because the absorption of light by chlorophyll ceases
It stops immediately due to the lack of CO ₂ availability in the dark
It continues for some time and then stops due to the depletion of ATP and NADPH
125649.sol: The biosynthetic phase (dark reaction) does not directly require light, but it is strictly dependent on the products of the photochemical phase (light reaction), which are ATP and NADPH. When a plant is suddenly moved to darkness, the light reaction stops immediately, halting the further production of ATP and NADPH. However, the biosynthetic phase will continue for a short duration using the existing pool of these molecules. Once the available ATP and NADPH are exhausted, sugar synthesis will also stop. Answer: It

125717.sol: Hill reaction is the light phase or photochemical phase of photosynthesis which consists of light driven splitting of water or photolysis, evolution of oxygen and synthesis of assimilatry power (ATP and NADPH). 126191.subject: Botany

126191.sol: During megasporogenesis, a single cell in the nucellus differentiates into a diploid Megaspore Mother Cell (MMC). The MMC undergoes meiotic division to form a linear Megaspore tetrad (four haploid megaspores). In a majority of angiosperms, three megaspores degenerate and one remains as the Functional megaspore. This functional megaspore then undergoes mitotic divisions to develop into the female gametophyte, which is the Embryo sac. 126712.sol: When a living tissue is dried and fully burnt, all carbon compounds are oxidised to gaseous forms (such as CO ₂ and water vapour) and escape. The remaining material, called ash, contains inorganic elements. Because Carbon and Hydrogen escape as gases during burning, they are not recovered in the ash, eliminating them as correct choices despite their abundance in living tissue. 127350.sol: The tracts of forests that are restored in the places of worship are called sacred groves

127507.subject: Botany

options: preparation of pure cellulose by removing lignin
treatment of wood with chemicals that break down cellulose
removal of oils present io the wood by treatment with suitable chemicals
removal of water from the wood by prolonged heating at approximately 50^ C .
127507.sol: Paper production is basically a two-step process in which a fibrous raw material is first converted into pulp, and then the pulp is converted into paper. The harvested wood is first processed so that the fibres are separated from the unusable fraction of the wood, the lignin. Related Theory The pulping process is aimed at removing lignin without loosed fibre strength, thereby freeing the fibres and removing impurities that cause discoloration and possible future disintegration of the paper. Hemicellulose plays an i

128776.subject: Zoology
128776.text: What is the major function of globulins in the plasma?
options: Involved in defense mechanisms of the body
Needed for clotting or coagulation of blood
128776.sol: Fibrinogens are needed for clotting or coagulation of blood. Globulins primarily are involved in defense mechanisms of the body and the albumins help in osmotic balance. Plasma also contains small amounts of minerals like Na+, Ca++, Mg++, HCO3 –, Cl–, etc. Glucose, amino acids, lipids, etc., are also present in the plasma as they are always in transit in the body. Factors for coagulation or clotting of blood are also present in the plasma in an inactive form. Plasma without the clotting factors is called serum.

129505.subject: Zoology
129505.text: What is the first step in urine formation in the human body?
129505.sol: : The first step in urine formation is the filtration of blood, which is carried out by the glomerulus and is called glomerular filtration . On an average, 1100-1200 ml of blood is filtered by the kidneys per minute which constitute roughly 1/5th of the blood pumped out by each ventricle of the heart in a minute. The glomerular capillary blood pressure causes filtration of blood through 3 layers, i.e., the endothelium of glomerular blood vessels, the epithelium of Bowman’s capsule and a basement membrane between th

129629.subject: Zoology
129629.text: Hormone Role in Kidney Function A. ADH (Antidiuretic Hormone) 1. Promotes sodium retention B. Aldosterone 2. Increases water reabsorption in kidneys C. ANP (Atrial Natriuretic Peptide) 3. Increases sodium excretion D. Renin 4. Converts angiotensinogen to angiotensin I
129629.sol: ADH increases water reabsorption in the kidneys. Aldosterone promotes sodium retention in the kidneys. ANP increases sodium excretion to reduce blood pressure. Renin converts angiotensinogen to angiotensin I as part of blood pressure regulation.

130476.subject: Zoology
130476.text: Which of the following represents the correct proximal to distal sequence of bones in the human forelimb?
130476.sol: The bones of the human forelimb from proximal (closest to the point of attachment) to distal (furthest from the point of attachment) are arranged as follows: Humerus (upper arm) Radius and Ulna (forearm) Carpals (wrist bones) Metacarpals (palm bones) Phalanges (digits). Thus, the correct proximal to distal sequence is Humerus-radius-carpals-metacarpals. The sequence Phalanges-metacarpals-carpals-radius is in distal to proximal order. 131405.subject: Zoology
131405.text: What is formed when a phosphate group is linked to OH of 5'C of a nucleoside?
131405.sol: A nucleotide has three components – a nitrogenous base, a pentose sugar (ribose in case of RNA, and deoxyribose for DNA), and a phosphate group. There are two types of nitrogenous bases – Purines (Adenine and Guanine), and Pyrimidines (Cytosine, Uracil and Thymine). Cytosine is common for both DNA and RNA and Thymine is present in DNA. 132607.text: Select the correct statement from the one's given below with respect to dihybrid cross.
options: tightly linked gene on the same chromosome show higher recombinations
genes for apert on same chromosomes show very few recombination
genes loosely linked on the same chromosomes show similar recombination as lightly linked ones
tightly linked genes on the same chromosomes show very few recombination
132607.sol: When two genes are close together on the same chromosome, they do not assort independently and are said to be linked and shows less frequency of recombination. Whereas genes located on different chromosomes assort independently and have a recombination frequency of (50 % ) called as less closely linked genes. So, the correct answer is 'Tightly linked genes on the same chromosome show very few recombinations'.

132904.sol: Statement A is correct because homology is based on common ancestry. 132940.text: Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R). Assertion (A): In human evolution, Homo erectus is placed chronologically after Homo habilis. Reason (R): The cranial capacity of Homo erectus was significantly smaller than that of Homo habilis. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
132940.sol: According to the fossil record of human evolution, Homo habilis appeared about 2 million years ago, followed by Homo erectus around 1.5 million years ago. Thus, the Assertion is true. The cranial capacity of Homo habilis was between 650-800 cc, whereas Homo erectus had a larger brain of around 900 cc. Therefore, the Reason is false because the cranial capacity of Homo erectus was larger, not smaller, than that of Homo habilis. Answer: (A) is true but (R) is false.

Colostrum is the yellowish fluid secreted by the mother during the initial days of lactation.

133809.subject: Zoology
133809.text: What is the main goal of biological control in agriculture?

To use toxic chemicals and pesticides
To create a complex system of checks and balances
133809.sol: In agriculture, there is a method of controlling pests that relies on natural predation rather than introduced chemicals. A key belief of the organic farmer is that biodiversity furthers health. The more variety a landscape has, the more sustainable it is. The organic farmer, therefore, works to create a system where the insects that are sometimes called pests are not eradicated, but instead are kept at manageable levels by a complex system of checks and balances within a living and vibrant ecosystem.

95501.text: Which one of the following classes is incorrectly matched with its two general characters? Class Characteristics (i) Amphibia Urinary bladder present, fertilization external (ii) Chondrichthyes Air bladder, operculum (iii) Cyclostomata Closed circulation, 6-15 pairs of gill slits (iv) Reptiles Cornified skin, direct development
95501.sol: Chondrichthyes are cartilaginous fish. They include shark, rays etc. These Chondrichthyes lack operculum, which is external covering on the gills and they also lack air bladder because of which they have to swim constantly to avoid sinking. Operculum and air bladder are found in all of the Osteichthyes (bony fish).

96354.sol: The sequential events that lead to formation of the new daughters by cell division and preceded by duplication of its genome is termed as cell cycle. 96593.subject: Botany
96593.text: Which factor/s is responsible for controlling the rate of decomposition?
96593.sol: Decomposition is largely oxygen requiring process, the rate of decomposition is controlled by the chemical composition of detritus and climatic factors. Warm humid condition promotes the growth of microbes thus increases the rate of decomposition. If detritus is rich in nitrogen and water-soluble substance than the rate of decomposition is fast, if detritus is rich in lignin, cellulose than the rate of decomposition is slow.

96639.sol: The movement and exchange of organic and inorganic matter between living and non-living component in a cyclical manner refers to nutrient cycle. These are also called as biogeochemical cycles as there is involvement of biotic and abiotic factors and chemical reactions. There are many important cycles which help in maintaining the biosphere like carbon cycle, nitrogen cycle etc. Calcium cycle, sodium cycle, phosphorous cycle, iron cycle, magnesium cycle, sulfur cycle are sedimentary cycles. 96673.subject: Botany
96673.text: Which of the following is a bacterium involved in denitrification?
96673.sol: Some bacteria such as Thiobacillus denitrificans, Pseudomonas aeruginosa, and Micrococcus denitrificans also occur in the soil which converts the nitrate and ammonia into atmospheric free elemental nitrogen. Such bacteria are called denitrifying bacteria and the process is called denitrification. These bacteria act very well in the soil where there are more water and less oxygen and there is a high level of the carbohydrate.

309392.text: Which of the following best explains why the reaction of a Grignard reagent with a carboxylic acid does not yield a secondary alcohol?
options: Grignard reagents exclusively react with aldehydes, ketones, esters, and epoxides.
The carboxylic acid is too sterically hindered for the Grignard reagent to attack.
The Grignard reagent acts as a strong base, so an acid-base reaction occurs preferentially.
The carboxylic acid is not electrophilic enough to undergo nucleophilic addition.
309392.sol: Grignard reagents ( RMgX ) are not only strong nucleophiles but also very strong bases. Carboxylic acids ( RCOOH ) contain a highly acidic proton. When a Grignard reagent is mixed with a carboxylic acid, an acid-base reaction occurs much faster than nucleophilic addition to the carbonyl carbon. The Grignard reagent deprotonates the carboxylic acid to form an alkane ( RH ) and a carboxylate salt ( RCOO⁻ , ⁺MgX ). 309459.text: Which of the following drugs is effective in the treatment of malaria?
309459.sol: Quinine is an alkaloid obtained from the bark of the cinchona tree. It is a well-known antimalarial drug and is highly effective in the treatment of malaria. Analgin and Aspirin are primarily used as analgesics and antipyretics. Salol (phenyl salicylate) is used as an intestinal antiseptic. Answer: Quinine

304471.text: The acceleration of the moon with respect to the earth is 0.0027 m/s ^2 , whereas the acceleration of an apple falling on the earth's surface is approximately 10 m/s ^2 . Taking the radius of the moon to be one fourth of the earth's radius, suppose the moon is momentarily stopped and then released so that it falls towards the earth. 304471.sol: The acceleration due to gravity on the surface of the earth is given by: g = GM_e R_e^2 = 10 m/s ^2 When the moon is just about to strike the earth, the distance between their centers is equal to the sum of their radii: r = R_e + R_m Given that the radius of the moon is one fourth of the earth's radius ( R_m = R_e 4 ): r = R_e + R_e 4 = 5R_e 4 The acceleration of the moon at this distance is: a = GM_e r^2 = GM_e ( 5R_e 4 )^2 = 16 25 GM_e R_e^2 Substituting the value of g : a = 16 25 10 = 6.4 m/s ^2 Answer: 6.4 m/s

304673.text: A sonometer wire carrying a 4 kg load vibrates in its fundamental mode when excited by a tuning fork of frequency 416 Hz . If the length of the wire between the bridges is subsequently doubled, what must the load be changed to in order to maintain the fundamental mode?

The tension T is provided by the load M , so T = Mg . Since the frequency f and linear mass density remain constant, we have M L = constant . Therefore, M₁ L₁ = M₂ L₂ . options: The limiting friction is always greater than the kinetic friction.
The static friction is always greater than the kinetic friction.
The coefficient of static friction is always greater than the coefficient of kinetic friction.
The limiting friction is never less than the static friction.

For any given pair of surfaces, the coefficient of static friction _ s is always greater than the coefficient of kinetic friction _ k . Since limiting friction is given by f_ L = _ s N and kinetic friction by f_ k = _ k N , it follows that f_ L > f_ k . Hence, limiting friction is always greater than kinetic friction. 304741.subject: Physics
304741.text: Consider a frame of reference that is fixed to the earth. Which of the following statements are correct regarding this frame?
options: It is defined as an inertial frame by default.
It cannot be an inertial frame since the earth revolves around the sun.
It cannot be an inertial frame since the earth rotates about its axis.
It qualifies as an inertial frame because Newton's laws are valid within it.
304741.sol: A frame of reference fixed to the earth is a non-inertial frame because the earth is an accelerating body. The earth rotates about its own axis, which provides a centripetal acceleration to any point on its surface. The earth also revolves around the sun, which involves a centripetal acceleration directed towards the sun. Since the frame is accelerating, it is non-inertial.
